title.en: Absolute, relative and percentage errors; combining errors

heading.en: How good is your value of g?

hook.en: You time a pendulum and get g = 9.6 m/s². Is that a good result or a poor one? Without an error estimate, nobody can say.

objectives.en: Find absolute, relative and percentage errors
Combine errors in sums, products and powers
Decide which measurement most needs care

narration.en: You time a pendulum and get g = 9.6 m/s². Is that a good result or a poor one? Without an error estimate, nobody can say.

title.en: Find absolute, relative and percentage errors
Combine errors in sums, products and powers
Decide which measurement most needs care

say.en: You time a pendulum and get g equals 9.6 metres per second squared. Is that a good result or a poor one? Without an error estimate, nobody can say. In this lesson: Find absolute, relative and percentage errors.
Combine errors in sums, products and powers.
Decide which measurement most needs care.

body.en: For readings $a_1 … a_n$ the best value is the mean $\bar a$. Each absolute error is $|a_i - \bar a|$ and the *mean absolute* error $\Delta a$ is their mean. The result is written $\bar a \pm \Delta a$. The relative error is $\Delta a/\bar a$, and the percentage error is $(\Delta a/\bar a) \times 100\%$.

narration.en: For readings $a_1 … a_n$ the best value is the mean $\bar a$. Each absolute error is $|a_i - \bar a|$ and the mean absolute error $\Delta a$ is their mean. The result is written $\bar a \pm \Delta a$. The relative error is $\Delta a/\bar a$, and the percentage error is $(\Delta a/\bar a) \times 100\%$.

say.en: For readings a 1... a n the best value is the mean bar a. Each absolute error is |a i minus bar a| and the mean absolute error delta a is their mean. The result is written bar a plus or minus delta a. The relative error is delta a over bar a, and the percentage error is (delta a over bar a) times 100 percent. Best value: the mean.
Report as a plus or minus delta a.
Percentage error equals delta a divided by a times 100.

body.en: For $Z = A \pm B$ the absolute *errors* add: $\Delta Z = \Delta A + \Delta B$. For $Z = AB$ or $A/B$ the relative errors add: $\Delta Z/Z = \Delta A/A + \Delta B/B$. For $Z = A^p B^q / C^r$: $\dfrac{\Delta Z}{Z} = p\dfrac{\Delta A}{A} + q\dfrac{\Delta B}{B} + r\dfrac{\Delta C}{C}$. Errors always add for the maximum error, even in a difference or a quotient.

points.en: Power p: multiply the *relative* error by p

narration.en: For $Z = A \pm B$ the absolute errors add: $\Delta Z = \Delta A + \Delta B$. For $Z = AB$ or $A/B$ the relative errors add: $\Delta Z/Z = \Delta A/A + \Delta B/B$. For $Z = A^p B^q / C^r$: $\dfrac{\Delta Z}{Z} = p\dfrac{\Delta A}{A} + q\dfrac{\Delta B}{B} + r\dfrac{\Delta C}{C}$. Errors always add for the maximum error, even in a difference or a quotient.

blocks.formula: \frac{\Delta Z}{Z} = p\frac{\Delta A}{A} + q\frac{\Delta B}{B} + r\frac{\Delta C}{C}

say.en: For Z equals A plus or minus B the absolute errors add: delta Z equals delta A plus delta B. For Z equals AB or A over B the relative errors add: delta Z over Z equals delta A over A plus delta B over B. For Z equals A to the power p B to the power q over C to the power r: delta Z over Z equals p delta A over A plus q delta B over B plus r delta C over C. Errors always add for the maximum error, even in a difference or a quotient. Sum or difference: add absolute errors.
Product or quotient: add relative errors.
Power p: multiply the relative error by p.

title.en: Error budget for g from a pendulum

narration.en: The percentage error in g is the error in L plus twice the error in T, because T is squared. Watch how timing more oscillations shrinks the T bar.

caption.en: g = 4π²L/T². Set the length and its error, the number of oscillations timed and the stopwatch least count. The bars show each measurement's share of the percentage error in g.

say.en: The percentage error in g is the error in L plus twice the error in T, because T is squared. Watch how timing more oscillations shrinks the T bar.
Write g as a product of powers: L to the power one, T to the power minus two.
Add the relative errors, each multiplied by its power. The minus sign is dropped: errors always add.
With L of 1 metre to 1 millimetre and 20 oscillations timed to 0.2 second, T is 2 seconds.
Errors in g equals 4 pi squaredL/T squared.

problem.en: Five readings of the diameter of a wire are 1.20, 1.22, 1.21, 1.19 and 1.18 mm. Find the mean, the mean absolute error and the percentage error.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Five readings of the diameter of a wire are 1.20, 1.22, 1.21, 1.19 and 1.18 mm. Find the mean, the mean absolute error and the percentage error.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Five readings of the diameter of a wire are 1.20, 1.22, 1.21, 1.19 and 1.18 millimetres. Find the mean, the mean absolute error and the percentage error.
Mean equals 6.00 over 5 equals 1.20 millimetres.
Absolute errors: 0, 0.02, 0.01, 0.01, 0.02; mean equals 0.06 over 5 is approximately 0.01 millimetres.
Percentage error equals 0.01 over 1.20 times 100 is approximately 0.83 percent.
So the answer is (1.20 plus or minus 0.01) mm, about 0.8 percent.

problem.en: The resistance R = V/I with V = (100 ± 5) V and I = (10 ± 0.2) A. Find R with its error.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. The resistance R = V/I with V = (100 ± 5) V and I = (10 ± 0.2) A. Find R with its error.

say.en: Let us solve this together. The resistance R equals V over I with V equals 100 plus or minus 5 V and I equals 10 plus or minus 0.2 A. Find R with its error.
R equals 100 over 10 equals 10 ohms.
delta R over R equals 5 over 100 plus 0.2 over 10 equals 0.05 plus 0.02 equals 0.07.
delta R equals 0.07 times 10 equals 0.7 ohms.
So the answer is 10 plus or minus 0.7 ohms, 7 percent.

narration.en: The length is one metre to a millimetre, the period is about two seconds, and the stopwatch reads to point two seconds. How many oscillations give a one percent error in g?

prompt.en: L = 1.00 m ± 1 mm, T ≈ 2.0 s and the stopwatch reads to 0.2 s. How many oscillations must you time so that the percentage error in g is 1%? Lock in your number.

hint.en: The error in T is 0.2 s divided by n periods of 2 s.

body.en: Whatever is raised to a power carries that power into the error: r³ triples the error in r, T² doubles the error in T. So measure the quantity with the highest power most carefully.

narration.en: The power rule. Whatever is raised to a power carries that power into the error: r³ triples the error in r, T² doubles the error in T. So measure the quantity with the highest power most carefully.

say.en: The power rule. Whatever is raised to a power carries that power into the error: r cubed triples the error in r, T squared doubles the error in T. So measure the quantity with the highest power most carefully.
